observations.text: Preview banner confirms history/analytics not saved.
Prediction fewer visits: Scattered pieces / One set kit / Same outcome; chose Same outcome.
Scattered at 4 locations: set=3 pieces and location visits=3; screenshot showed numbered containers, not identifiable bedding pieces.
One set kit at 4 locations changed visits to 1; reveal enabled immediately after layout switch despite prompt also saying vary input.
Attempted Locations=1 rejected by browser input; Home key moved slider from 4 to supported minimum 3. Kit remained 1; switched scattered at 3 locations: visits 3.

Reveal: “Not quite: it was ‘One set kit’”; counts separate locations, not seconds; chosen set pieces together replace visits with one; separating unlike sets preserves identification; not proof every object should be grouped.

prediction.reason: Choice is clear but “one set kit” strongly cues answer and generic setup lacks tangible pieces.

interaction.reason: Layout toggle changes visits, but tested location change 4→3 leaves each result unchanged.

payoff.reason: Reveal ties observed three-versus-one visits to grouping and explicitly limits scope.

clarity.reason: Instructions are usable but “vary input” lacks a demonstrated effect and essential pieces are not visible.

transfer.reason: Grouping principle includes conditions/trade-off but no concrete second everyday application.

accessibility.reason: No sufficient multi-mode accessibility checks; D slider Home key is only a partial keyboard observation.
evidence: Observed DOM accessible names, desktop screenshots; no comprehensive check.

surprise.reason: Expected grouping advantage is largely signalled by labels despite chosen Same outcome.

visualExplanation.reason: Containers and numeric visits support explanation but do not visibly show three pieces being bundled.

playfulness.reason: Reversible layout and slider permit a narrow comparison.

practicalValue.reason: Grouping complete sets enables a concrete household retrieval action.

depth.reason: One grouping comparison plus an identification trade-off; tested location variation adds little.

complexity.reason: Compare three visits to one using familiar grouping; no technical prerequisites.
complexity.boundary: Everyday numeracy, simple charts, comparing numbers and familiar household objects; no domain theory assumed.

whyCool: Switching from scattered pieces to one kit changes the visit counter from three to one.
caveat: The tested Locations slider does not change retrieval counts; no identifiable pillowcase or pieces observed.
